title: Prophets of the Bible
intro: A prophet in Scripture is one who speaks for God (Exod 7:1 makes Aaron Moses' "prophet"; Deut 18:18 puts God's words in the prophet's mouth). The "major" and "minor" labels refer to length, not importance: the Twelve minor prophets formed a single scroll in the Hebrew canon. Many prophets wrote nothing that survives, and Scripture also names false prophets, tested by fulfilment and faithfulness (Deut 13:1-5; Deut 18:20-22). Dates are approximate ministry spans, BC as negative.

entries.name: Isaiah
entries.note: Son of Amoz; prophesied in Jerusalem under Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah. Critical scholarship assigns chapters 40-66 to later exilic and post-exilic prophets.

entries.name: Jeremiah
entries.note: Priest from Anathoth; ministry from Josiah's thirteenth year to after the fall of Jerusalem; traditionally also linked to Lamentations.

entries.name: Ezekiel
entries.note: Priest exiled to Babylon in 597 BC; called by the Chebar canal in the fifth year of Jehoiachin's captivity.

entries.name: Daniel
entries.note: Exile in the Babylonian and Persian courts. Christian Bibles place his book with the prophets; the Hebrew Bible places it among the Writings. Jesus calls him "Daniel the prophet".

entries.name: Hosea
entries.note: Prophet to the northern kingdom whose marriage to Gomer enacts God's faithfulness to unfaithful Israel.

entries.name: Joel
entries.note: Son of Pethuel; the book carries no date and estimates range from the 9th to the 4th century BC. Peter cites his outpouring prophecy at Pentecost.

entries.name: Amos
entries.note: Herdsman from Tekoa in Judah sent to prophesy at Bethel under Jeroboam II.

entries.name: Obadiah
entries.note: Oracle against Edom, most often dated after Jerusalem's fall in 586 BC; earlier dates are also argued.

entries.name: Jonah
entries.note: Son of Amittai from Gath-hepher, who prophesied Israel's expansion under Jeroboam II; the book narrates his mission to Nineveh.

entries.name: Micah
entries.note: From Moresheth; prophesied under Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah; remembered a century later for sparing Jeremiah.

entries.name: Nahum
entries.note: The Elkoshite; foretells Nineveh's fall (612 BC) after the fall of Thebes (663 BC) mentioned in Nah 3:8.

entries.name: Habakkuk
entries.note: Questions God about injustice and the rise of the Chaldeans; usually dated near 605 BC.

entries.name: Zephaniah
entries.note: Prophesied in the days of Josiah; descended from "Hizkiah".

entries.name: Haggai
entries.note: Dated precisely to 520 BC, urging the returned exiles to rebuild the temple.

entries.name: Zechariah
entries.note: Son of Berechiah, grandson of Iddo; began two months after Haggai. Many scholars treat chapters 9-14 as a later collection.

entries.name: Malachi
entries.note: Last of the Twelve, usually dated about the time of Nehemiah. The name means "my messenger" and some take it as a title rather than a personal name.

entries.name: Enoch
entries.note: Jude cites Enoch, "the seventh from Adam", as prophesying the Lord's coming with his saints (the wording matches *1 Enoch* 1:9).

entries.name: Abraham
entries.note: God tells Abimelech that Abraham "is a prophet" who will pray for him.

entries.name: Moses
entries.note: The paradigm prophet, with whom God spoke face to face; promised a prophet like himself.

entries.name: Aaron
entries.note: Made Moses' "prophet" before Pharaoh.

entries.name: Miriam
entries.note: Called "the prophetess"; leads the women in song after the sea crossing.

entries.name: Eldad and Medad
entries.note: Two elders who prophesied in the camp; Moses wishes all the LORD's people were prophets.

entries.name: Deborah
entries.note: Prophetess and judge who summons Barak against Sisera.

entries.name: Samuel
entries.note: Recognised from Dan to Beersheba as a prophet of the LORD; also called "the seer".

entries.name: Gad
entries.note: David's seer, who advised him in the wilderness and confronted him after the census.

entries.name: Nathan
entries.note: Court prophet who delivers the Davidic covenant and rebukes David over Bathsheba.

entries.name: Ahijah the Shilonite
entries.note: Tears his garment into twelve pieces to announce Jeroboam's ten tribes; later foretells the fall of his house.

entries.name: Shemaiah
entries.note: Man of God who forbids Rehoboam to fight the northern tribes.

entries.name: The man of God from Judah
entries.note: Prophesies against Jeroboam's altar at Bethel, naming Josiah; dies for disobeying God's command.

entries.name: Jehu son of Hanani
entries.note: Prophesies against Baasha and rebukes Jehoshaphat for helping Ahab.

entries.name: Hanani the seer
entries.note: Rebukes Asa for relying on Syria and is imprisoned.

entries.name: Azariah son of Oded
entries.note: Encourages Asa to reform: "the LORD is with you, while ye be with him".

entries.name: Oded
entries.note: Prophet in Samaria who persuades Israel's army to release captives from Judah.

entries.name: Elijah
entries.note: The Tishbite; confronts Ahab and the prophets of Baal on Carmel and is taken up in a whirlwind.

entries.name: Elisha
entries.note: Elijah's successor, with a double portion of his spirit; many miracles.

entries.name: Micaiah son of Imlah
entries.note: Speaks only what the LORD says and foretells Ahab's death against four hundred prophets.

entries.name: Jahaziel
entries.note: A Levite on whom the Spirit comes, assuring Jehoshaphat "the battle is not yours, but God's".

entries.name: Zechariah son of Jehoiada
entries.note: Priest stoned in the temple court for rebuking Judah under Joash; probably the Zacharias Jesus mentions.

entries.name: Huldah
entries.note: Prophetess consulted by Josiah's officials about the rediscovered book of the law.

entries.name: Uriah son of Shemaiah
entries.note: Prophesied like Jeremiah; fled to Egypt but was extradited and killed by Jehoiakim.

entries.name: Isaiah's wife
entries.note: Called "the prophetess"; mother of Maher-shalal-hash-baz.

entries.name: Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun
entries.note: Levitical musicians who "prophesy" with harps, psalteries and cymbals.

entries.name: Jesus
entries.note: Recognised as "a prophet mighty in deed and word" and identified with the prophet like Moses.

entries.name: Zechariah the priest
entries.note: Filled with the Holy Spirit, he prophesies the Benedictus at John's birth.

entries.name: Simeon
entries.note: Not called a prophet, but the Holy Spirit is upon him and he speaks prophetically over the infant Jesus.

entries.name: Anna
entries.note: Prophetess of the tribe of Asher who serves in the temple with fasting and prayer.

entries.name: John the Baptist
entries.note: Jesus calls him a prophet and "much more than a prophet".

entries.name: Prophets and teachers at Antioch
entries.note: Barnabas, Simeon called Niger, Lucius of Cyrene, Manaen and Saul.

entries.name: Agabus
entries.note: Foretells a famine under Claudius and Paul's binding in Jerusalem.

entries.name: Judas Barsabbas and Silas
entries.note: Being prophets, they exhort and strengthen the believers at Antioch.

entries.name: Philip's four daughters
entries.note: Virgins who prophesied, living in Caesarea.

entries.name: John of Patmos
entries.note: Calls Revelation "this prophecy"; the angel calls him a fellow servant "of thy brethren the prophets".

entries.name: Balaam
entries.note: A diviner from Pethor hired to curse Israel who is made to bless it; the NT treats him as a model of greed and of leading Israel into sin.

entries.name: The prophets of Baal and Asherah
entries.note: Four hundred and fifty prophets of Baal (and four hundred of Asherah) who eat at Jezebel's table; defeated on Carmel.

entries.name: The old prophet of Bethel
entries.note: Lies to the man of God from Judah, claiming an angelic message.

entries.name: Zedekiah son of Chenaanah
entries.note: Makes iron horns and promises Ahab victory; strikes Micaiah.

entries.name: Hananiah son of Azur
entries.note: Breaks Jeremiah's yoke and predicts return within two years; dies that year as Jeremiah foretold.

entries.name: Ahab son of Kolaiah and Zedekiah son of Maaseiah
entries.note: Prophesy lies in Babylon in the LORD's name; Jeremiah foretells their execution by Nebuchadnezzar.

entries.name: Shemaiah the Nehelamite
entries.note: Writes from Babylon against Jeremiah; condemned for teaching rebellion.

entries.name: Noadiah and Shemaiah son of Delaiah
entries.note: Hired to frighten Nehemiah and stop the wall-building.

entries.name: Bar-Jesus (Elymas)
entries.note: A Jewish sorcerer and false prophet on Cyprus, struck blind when he opposes Paul.

entries.name: "Jezebel" of Thyatira
entries.note: A woman "which calleth herself a prophetess" and teaches compromise with idolatry; the name is probably symbolic.

entries.name: The false prophet of Revelation
entries.note: The beast from the earth who works signs for the first beast; cast into the lake of fire.

title: Apostles
intro:
"Apostle" (Greek *apostolos*) means one sent with authority. The New Testament uses it narrowly for the Twelve and Paul, who saw the risen Lord and were commissioned by him (Acts 1:21-22; 1 Cor 9:1), and more broadly for others sent out by churches (2 Cor 8:23; Phil 2:25). The four lists of the Twelve agree on Peter first and Judas Iscariot last but vary in names and order.

Traditions read the office differently. Catholic and Orthodox churches hold that the apostles' oversight continues through bishops in apostolic succession. Most Protestant traditions treat the apostles as a unique, foundational and unrepeatable office (Eph 2:20), with apostolicity located in apostolic teaching. Many Pentecostal and charismatic churches recognise an ongoing apostolic ministry of church-planting and oversight (Eph 4:11).

entries.name: Simon Peter
entries.note: Listed first in every list. Also called Cephas (Aramaic, "rock"), Simon son of Jonas, and Simeon (Acts 15:14).

entries.name: Andrew
entries.note: Peter's brother; second in Matthew and Luke, fourth in Mark and Acts.

entries.name: James son of Zebedee
entries.note: With his brother named "Boanerges, sons of thunder" (Mark 3:17); first of the Twelve to be martyred.

entries.name: John son of Zebedee
entries.note: Brother of James; traditionally the beloved disciple and author of the Gospel, letters and Revelation.

entries.name: Philip
entries.note: From Bethsaida; fifth in every list.

entries.name: Bartholomew
entries.note: Appears only in the lists, always paired with Philip; since the 9th century often identified with Nathanael of John's Gospel (tradition).

entries.name: Thomas
entries.note: Called Didymus, "the twin"; doubts and then confesses the risen Jesus.

entries.name: Matthew
entries.note: The tax collector ("the publican" in Matthew's own list); called Levi son of Alphaeus in Mark and Luke.

entries.name: James son of Alphaeus
entries.note: Ninth in every list; often identified with "James the less" (Mark 15:40), though this is uncertain.

entries.name: Thaddaeus / Judas of James
entries.note: Matthew (KJV) has "Lebbaeus, whose surname was Thaddaeus" and Mark "Thaddaeus"; Luke and Acts have "Judas [son or brother] of James", the "Judas not Iscariot" of John 14:22. Most harmonise these as one man.

entries.name: Simon the Zealot
entries.note: Called "the Canaanite" in Matthew and Mark (from Aramaic *qan'an*, zealous) and "Zelotes" in Luke and Acts.

entries.name: Judas Iscariot
entries.note: Always last and marked as the betrayer; absent from Acts 1:13, his death and replacement follow.

entries.name: Matthias
entries.note: Chosen by lot to replace Judas from those who had accompanied Jesus from John's baptism to the ascension.

entries.name: Paul
entries.note: Apostle to the Gentiles "born out of due time", commissioned by the risen Christ, not by men.

entries.name: Barnabas
entries.note: Called an apostle alongside Paul at Lystra.

entries.name: James the Lord's brother
entries.note: Paul says he saw none of the other apostles "save James the Lord's brother"; whether this includes James among the apostles is debated.

entries.name: Andronicus
entries.note: "Of note among the apostles": most read this as an apostle in the broader sense; others read "well known to the apostles".

entries.name: Junia
entries.note: Greeted with Andronicus. Early interpreters such as Chrysostom read Junia as a woman apostle; some later readers took the name as masculine "Junias", and the phrase itself is debated as above.

entries.name: Silas (Silvanus) and Timothy
entries.note: Co-senders of 1 Thessalonians, which says "we might have been burdensome, as the apostles of Christ"; whether the plural includes them is debated.

entries.name: Apollos (possibly)
entries.note: Paul applies the example of himself and Apollos and then speaks of "us the apostles"; some include Apollos, others limit it to Paul.

entries.name: Epaphroditus
entries.note: Called the Philippians' "messenger" (Greek *apostolos*), an envoy of a church rather than an apostle of Christ.

entries.name: Jesus
entries.note: Hebrews calls Jesus "the Apostle and High Priest of our profession", the one sent by the Father.

title: Judges of Israel
intro: Between Joshua and Saul, God raised up "judges" (Hebrew *shophetim*), deliverers and leaders rather than primarily courtroom officials (Judg 2:16-19). Judges presents six "major" judges with full stories and six "minor" judges in short notices; Eli and Samuel close the period in 1 Samuel. The book's year-numbers total over 400 if added in sequence, so most chronologies assume overlapping regional judgeships. Verdicts summarise how the narrative presents each figure.

entries.name: Othniel
entries.note: Caleb's nephew; the Spirit comes on him and he defeats Cushan-rishathaim. The land rests forty years.

entries.name: Ehud
entries.note: Left-handed Benjamite who assassinates Eglon of Moab; eighty years of rest.

entries.name: Shamgar
entries.note: Son of Anath; kills six hundred Philistines with an ox goad.

entries.name: Deborah
entries.note: Prophetess judging under her palm tree; with Barak defeats Sisera. Forty years of rest.

entries.name: Barak
entries.note: Commander who leads the battle at Deborah's summons; listed among the faithful in Hebrews.

entries.name: Gideon (Jerubbaal)
entries.note: Defeats Midian with three hundred men; refuses kingship but makes an ephod that becomes a snare. Forty years of rest.

entries.name: Abimelech
entries.note: Gideon's son who murders seventy brothers and rules Shechem three years as king; not called a judge, but part of the cycle.

entries.name: Tola
entries.note: Of Issachar; judged twenty-three years.

entries.name: Jair
entries.note: Gileadite with thirty sons riding thirty donkeys; judged twenty-two years.

entries.name: Jephthah
entries.note: Gileadite outcast who defeats Ammon; his rash vow costs his daughter. Judged six years.

entries.name: Ibzan
entries.note: Of Bethlehem; thirty sons and thirty daughters; judged seven years.

entries.name: Elon
entries.note: Zebulunite; judged ten years.

entries.name: Abdon
entries.note: Pirathonite with forty sons and thirty grandsons; judged eight years.

entries.name: Samson
entries.note: Nazirite from birth; begins to deliver Israel from the Philistines, undone by Delilah, dies destroying the temple of Dagon. Judged twenty years.

entries.name: Eli
entries.note: Priest at Shiloh who judged Israel forty years; failed to restrain his sons.

entries.name: Samuel
entries.note: Last judge and first of the prophets after Moses (Acts 13:20); judges Israel on an annual circuit and anoints the first two kings.

entries.name: Joel and Abijah
entries.note: Samuel's sons, made judges at Beersheba; they take bribes, prompting Israel to ask for a king.

title: Kings of the United Monarchy
intro: Israel asked Samuel for a king "like all the nations" (1 Sam 8:5). Saul, David and Solomon ruled all twelve tribes; Ish-bosheth briefly held the north against David. Dates are conventional approximations (Saul's reign length is uncertain in the Hebrew text of 1 Sam 13:1; Acts 13:21 gives forty years). The division follows Solomon's death, c. 931/930 BC.

entries.name: Saul
entries.note: Benjamite anointed by Samuel; rejected for disobedience and dies on Mount Gilboa. Chronicles says he died for his unfaithfulness.

entries.name: Ish-bosheth
entries.note: Saul's son, made king over the northern tribes by Abner for two years; murdered by his own captains.

entries.name: David
entries.note: Reigned seven and a half years in Hebron and thirty-three in Jerusalem; the text's measure of a good king, "save only in the matter of Uriah".

entries.name: Solomon
entries.note: Builds the temple and is renowned for wisdom; in old age his foreign wives turn his heart to other gods and he "did evil in the sight of the LORD".

title: Kings of Israel (Northern Kingdom)
intro: The northern kingdom lasted about two centuries, from Jeroboam I (c. 931/930 BC) to the fall of Samaria to Assyria (722 BC), through nine dynasties and several coups. Dates follow Edwin Thiele's chronology (*The Mysterious Numbers of the Hebrew Kings*), with coregencies and overlapping claims; other systems differ by a few years. Kings records a verdict for nearly every king, usually "did evil in the sight of the LORD" and walked in the sins of Jeroboam.

entries.name: Jeroboam I
entries.note: Sets up golden calves at Bethel and Dan, "the sin of Jeroboam" by which later kings are measured.

entries.name: Nadab
entries.note: Son of Jeroboam; assassinated by Baasha after two years.

entries.name: Baasha
entries.note: Wipes out Jeroboam's house yet walks in his ways.

entries.name: Elah
entries.note: Killed while drunk by Zimri; condemned with Baasha for their sins.

entries.name: Zimri
entries.note: Reigns seven days and burns the palace over himself at Tirzah.

entries.name: Tibni
entries.note: Rival claimant supported by half the people against Omri; no verdict given.

entries.name: Omri
entries.note: Builds Samaria as capital; "did worse than all that were before him". Assyrian records call Israel "the house of Omri".

entries.name: Ahab
entries.note: Marries Jezebel and promotes Baal worship; "did more to provoke the LORD" than all before him.

entries.name: Ahaziah
entries.note: Son of Ahab; consults Baal-zebub after a fall.

entries.name: Joram (Jehoram)
entries.note: Did evil "but not like his father", removing Baal's pillar; killed by Jehu.

entries.name: Jehu
entries.note: Destroys Ahab's house and Baal worship and is commended, but keeps Jeroboam's calves.

entries.name: Jehoahaz
entries.note: Oppressed by Syria; seeks the LORD, who gives Israel a saviour.

entries.name: Jehoash (Joash)
entries.note: Weeps over the dying Elisha; defeats Amaziah of Judah.

entries.name: Jeroboam II
entries.note: Restores Israel's borders as Jonah foretold; the era of Amos and Hosea.

entries.name: Zechariah
entries.note: Reigns six months; the end of Jehu's dynasty as foretold.

entries.name: Shallum
entries.note: Assassinates Zechariah and reigns one month; no verdict given.

entries.name: Menahem
entries.note: Pays tribute to Pul (Tiglath-pileser III) of Assyria.

entries.name: Pekahiah
entries.note: Son of Menahem; assassinated by Pekah.

entries.name: Pekah
entries.note: Thiele dates his reign from a rival claim in Gilead in 752; allies with Syria against Judah and loses territory to Assyria.

entries.name: Hoshea
entries.note: Did evil "but not as the kings of Israel that were before him"; rebels against Assyria, and Samaria falls.

title: Kings of Judah (Southern Kingdom)
intro: Judah kept the Davidic line in Jerusalem from Rehoboam (c. 931/930 BC) to the Babylonian destruction (586 BC), interrupted only by Athaliah's usurpation. Dates follow Thiele's chronology, including coregencies (so reigns overlap). The verdict reflects the narrator's formula: "did that which was right in the sight of the LORD" (good) or "did evil" (evil); qualifications are noted.

entries.name: Rehoboam
entries.note: His harsh answer splits the kingdom; Kings says Judah did evil in his reign and Chronicles that "he did evil".

entries.name: Abijah (Abijam)
entries.note: Walked in all the sins of his father; Chronicles records his speech against Jeroboam.

entries.name: Asa
entries.note: Did right as David did and removed idols, though the high places remained; later relied on Syria and physicians.

entries.name: Jehoshaphat
entries.note: Did right, sending teachers of the law, but allied with Ahab's house.

entries.name: Jehoram
entries.note: Married Ahab's daughter and walked in the way of the kings of Israel.

entries.name: Ahaziah
entries.note: Son of Athaliah; killed by Jehu while visiting Joram.

entries.name: Athaliah
entries.note: The only queen to rule Judah in her own right; no regnal formula is given, but Chronicles calls her "that wicked woman".

entries.name: Joash (Jehoash)
entries.note: Did right "all his days wherein Jehoiada the priest instructed him"; Chronicles reports his later apostasy and the stoning of Zechariah.

entries.name: Amaziah
entries.note: Did right, "yet not like David"; brought Edomite gods home and was defeated by Jehoash of Israel.

entries.name: Uzziah (Azariah)
entries.note: Did right and prospered; struck with leprosy after burning incense in the temple.

entries.name: Jotham
entries.note: Did right, though the people still sacrificed at high places.

entries.name: Ahaz
entries.note: Made his son pass through the fire and appealed to Assyria; the king of Isaiah 7.

entries.name: Hezekiah
entries.note: Did right according to all that David did; trusted the LORD so that none was like him.

entries.name: Manasseh
entries.note: The longest and worst reign by the narrator's account; Chronicles adds his captivity and repentance.

entries.name: Amon
entries.note: Did evil as his father; assassinated by his servants.

entries.name: Josiah
entries.note: Did right and turned to the LORD with all his heart; reforms after the law book is found; killed at Megiddo.

entries.name: Jehoahaz (Shallum)
entries.note: Reigned three months before Pharaoh Necho deposed him.

entries.name: Jehoiakim (Eliakim)
entries.note: Necho's appointee; burned Jeremiah's scroll.

entries.name: Jehoiachin (Jeconiah)
entries.note: Reigned three months, then exiled to Babylon; later released by Evil-merodach.

entries.name: Zedekiah (Mattaniah)
entries.note: Did evil and would not heed Jeremiah; rebelled against Babylon and was blinded as Jerusalem fell.

title: High Priests
intro: The high priesthood began with Aaron and passed through his sons Eleazar and Ithamar. Under Solomon it settled in the line of Zadok, which returned from exile with Joshua (Jeshua). In the Hasmonean and Roman periods appointment became political: Herod and the Roman governors installed and removed high priests at will, and the house of Annas dominated in Jesus' day. Hebrews presents Jesus as the great high priest after the order of Melchizedek. Only priests named in Scripture are listed; dates are approximate.

entries.name: Melchizedek
entries.note: King of Salem and "priest of the most high God" who blesses Abram; Hebrews makes him a type of Christ's priesthood.

entries.name: Aaron
entries.note: Consecrated with his sons as the first high priest; wears the ephod and breastplate.

entries.name: Eleazar
entries.note: Succeeds Aaron on Mount Hor; assists Joshua in dividing the land.

entries.name: Phinehas
entries.note: Zealous for God at Baal-peor and given a covenant of perpetual priesthood; ministers before the ark in the days of the judges.

entries.name: Eli
entries.note: Priest at Shiloh, of the line of Ithamar (inferred from 1 Chr 24:3 and 1 Kgs 2:27); his house is judged.

entries.name: Ahimelech
entries.note: Priest at Nob who gives David the showbread and Goliath's sword; killed with the priests by Doeg on Saul's order.

entries.name: Abiathar
entries.note: Sole survivor of Nob, David's priest; deposed by Solomon for backing Adonijah, fulfilling the word against Eli's house. Jesus names him in Mark 2:26.

entries.name: Zadok
entries.note: Priest alongside Abiathar under David; anoints Solomon and becomes sole chief priest, founding the Zadokite line.

entries.name: Jehoiada
entries.note: Hides the young Joash from Athaliah, crowns him and leads a covenant renewal; buried among the kings.

entries.name: Azariah
entries.note: Withstands King Uzziah when he tries to burn incense in the temple.

entries.name: Urijah
entries.note: Builds a copy of the Damascus altar at King Ahaz's command; also a witness for Isaiah.

entries.name: Hilkiah
entries.note: Finds the book of the law in the temple during Josiah's repairs.

entries.name: Seraiah
entries.note: Chief priest when Jerusalem fell; executed by Nebuchadnezzar at Riblah.

entries.name: Jehozadak (Josedech)
entries.note: Son of Seraiah, carried into exile.

entries.name: Joshua (Jeshua)
entries.note: First high priest after the return; rebuilds the altar with Zerubbabel and is crowned symbolically in Zechariah's vision.

entries.name: Eliashib
entries.note: High priest in Nehemiah's day; builds the sheep gate but later gives Tobiah a temple chamber.

entries.name: Annas
entries.note: Appointed by Quirinius in AD 6 and deposed in AD 15 (Josephus), yet still called high priest in the Gospels and Acts; Jesus is first brought to him.

entries.name: Caiaphas
entries.note: Annas' son-in-law and high priest AD 18-36; presides at Jesus' hearing before the council.

entries.name: Ananias son of Nedebaeus
entries.note: Orders Paul struck at his hearing and later prosecutes him before Felix; high priest c. AD 47-59 (Josephus).

entries.name: Jesus
entries.note: Hebrews presents Jesus as the great high priest, after the order of Melchizedek, who offered himself once for all.

title: Herodian Rulers
intro: The Herodian dynasty ruled Judea and its neighbours as Roman client kings and tetrarchs from 37 BC to the late first century AD. The New Testament often calls several of them simply "Herod", so identifying each depends on context and on the Jewish historian Josephus. Family links below beyond what the text states come from Josephus.

entries.name: Herod the Great
entries.note: King of Judea, rebuilder of the temple; orders the massacre at Bethlehem. Died 4 BC (most common dating).

entries.name: Archelaus
entries.note: Son of Herod; ethnarch of Judea, Samaria and Idumea until deposed by Augustus; Joseph avoids Judea because of him.

entries.name: Herod Antipas
entries.note: Tetrarch of Galilee and Perea; beheads John the Baptist and sees Jesus at his trial. Exiled AD 39.

entries.name: Philip the tetrarch
entries.note: Tetrarch of Ituraea and Trachonitis; rebuilt Caesarea Philippi.

entries.name: Philip, first husband of Herodias
entries.note: Called "his brother Philip" in Mark; Josephus calls Herodias' first husband Herod (son of Mariamne II), so many think he is a different man from the tetrarch.

entries.name: Herodias
entries.note: Granddaughter of Herod the Great; leaves her husband for Antipas and engineers John's death.

entries.name: Daughter of Herodias
entries.note: Dances before Antipas and asks for John's head; Josephus names Herodias' daughter Salome.

entries.name: Herod Agrippa I
entries.note: Grandson of Herod; king over Judea AD 41-44. Kills James, imprisons Peter, and dies struck by an angel at Caesarea.

entries.name: Herod Agrippa II
entries.note: Son of Agrippa I; hears Paul's defence with Bernice at Caesarea.

entries.name: Bernice
entries.note: Sister of Agrippa II, present at Paul's hearing.

entries.name: Drusilla
entries.note: Jewish wife of the governor Felix, daughter of Agrippa I (Josephus); hears Paul with Felix.

title: Roman Emperors and Officials
intro: Rome is the backdrop of the whole New Testament. Emperors set censuses and expelled populations; governors (prefects and procurators) held capital jurisdiction in Judea; proconsuls governed senatorial provinces such as Cyprus and Achaia. Many of these figures are independently attested in inscriptions, coins and in Josephus, Tacitus and Suetonius.

entries.name: Augustus
entries.note: First emperor; his decree of enrolment brings Joseph and Mary to Bethlehem.

entries.name: Tiberius
entries.note: His fifteenth year dates John the Baptist's ministry; the Caesar on the tribute coin.

entries.name: Claudius
entries.note: A famine occurs in his reign; he expels the Jews from Rome (c. AD 49), bringing Aquila and Priscilla to Corinth.

entries.name: Nero
entries.note: Not named, but the "Caesar" to whom Paul appeals; tradition places the deaths of Peter and Paul under him.

entries.name: Quirinius
entries.note: Governor of Syria at the time of "the first enrolment". Josephus dates his census to AD 6; how it fits Jesus' birth under Herod is debated (an earlier census, an earlier office, or a different reading of "first").

entries.name: Pontius Pilate
entries.note: Prefect of Judea who sentences Jesus; attested by the Caesarea "Pilate Stone".

entries.name: Antonius Felix
entries.note: Procurator of Judea who keeps Paul in custody two years hoping for a bribe.

entries.name: Porcius Festus
entries.note: Succeeds Felix; hears Paul's appeal to Caesar and consults Agrippa II. Died in office c. AD 62.

entries.name: Sergius Paulus
entries.note: Proconsul of Cyprus, "a prudent man", who believes after Elymas is blinded.

entries.name: Gallio
entries.note: Proconsul of Achaia who dismisses the Jewish case against Paul; the Delphi inscription dates his term to c. AD 51-52, a key anchor for Pauline chronology.

entries.name: Claudius Lysias
entries.note: Tribune in Jerusalem who rescues Paul from the mob and sends him to Felix.

entries.name: Centurion of Capernaum
entries.note: His faith amazes Jesus, who heals his servant.

entries.name: Centurion at the cross
entries.note: Confesses "Truly this man was the Son of God".

entries.name: Cornelius
entries.note: Centurion of the Italian band at Caesarea, the first named Gentile convert in Acts.

entries.name: Julius
entries.note: Centurion of Augustus' band who escorts Paul to Rome and spares the prisoners in the shipwreck.

entries.name: Publius
entries.note: Chief man of Malta who hosts Paul; Paul heals his father.

entries.name: Magistrates of Philippi
entries.note: Beat and jail Paul and Silas, then apologise on learning they are Roman citizens.

entries.name: Town clerk of Ephesus
entries.note: Quiets the riot in the theatre.

entries.name: Erastus
entries.note: City treasurer (chamberlain) of Corinth who sends greetings; a Corinthian inscription names an aedile Erastus, perhaps the same man.

title: Women of the Bible
intro: Scripture names some 170 women and includes many unnamed women whose actions shape the story. This roster gathers about sixty: matriarchs, prophetesses, judges, queens, disciples, patrons and church leaders. Notes describe what the text says; how traditions have read figures such as Mary Magdalene or Junia is noted where it matters.

entries.name: Eve
entries.note: The first woman, "mother of all living"; deceived by the serpent.

entries.name: Sarah
entries.note: Wife of Abraham; bears Isaac at ninety; held up as an example of faith and hope.

entries.name: Hagar
entries.note: Egyptian servant who bears Ishmael and names God "Thou God seest me".

entries.name: Lot's wife
entries.note: Looks back toward Sodom and becomes a pillar of salt; Jesus says "Remember Lot's wife".

entries.name: Rebekah
entries.note: Chosen for Isaac at the well; helps Jacob gain the blessing.

entries.name: Leah
entries.note: Jacob's first wife, mother of Levi and Judah.

entries.name: Rachel
entries.note: Jacob's beloved wife, mother of Joseph and Benjamin; Jeremiah pictures her weeping for her children.

entries.name: Dinah
entries.note: Jacob's daughter, violated at Shechem; her brothers take revenge.

entries.name: Tamar (Judah's daughter-in-law)
entries.note: Secures her right to an heir by disguise; ancestor of David and Jesus.

entries.name: Shiphrah and Puah
entries.note: Hebrew midwives who fear God and defy Pharaoh's order to kill newborn boys.

entries.name: Jochebed
entries.note: Mother of Moses, Aaron and Miriam; hides the infant Moses.

entries.name: Pharaoh's daughter
entries.note: Rescues and adopts Moses.

entries.name: Miriam
entries.note: Prophetess who leads Israel's women in song at the sea.

entries.name: Zipporah
entries.note: Midianite wife of Moses who circumcises their son.

entries.name: Daughters of Zelophehad
entries.note: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah and Tirzah petition Moses and win the right to inherit.

entries.name: Rahab
entries.note: Canaanite of Jericho who hides the spies; commended for faith and works.

entries.name: Achsah
entries.note: Caleb's daughter who asks her father for springs of water.

entries.name: Deborah
entries.note: Prophetess and judge; leads Israel against Sisera.

entries.name: Jael
entries.note: Kills Sisera with a tent peg; "blessed above women".

entries.name: Jephthah's daughter
entries.note: Meets her father with timbrels and becomes the victim of his vow; mourned yearly.

entries.name: Samson's mother
entries.note: Wife of Manoah, visited by the angel and told to keep the Nazirite rule.

entries.name: Delilah
entries.note: Betrays Samson to the Philistines for silver.

entries.name: Naomi
entries.note: Bereaved widow who returns from Moab and guides Ruth.

entries.name: Ruth
entries.note: Moabite who pledges loyalty to Naomi and Naomi's God; great-grandmother of David.

entries.name: Orpah
entries.note: Ruth's sister-in-law who returns to her people.

entries.name: Hannah
entries.note: Prays for a son, dedicates Samuel and sings a song of reversal.

entries.name: Michal
entries.note: Saul's daughter and David's wife; saves his life and later despises him.

entries.name: Abigail
entries.note: Wise wife of Nabal who averts David's vengeance; later David's wife.

entries.name: The medium of Endor
entries.note: Consulted by Saul to bring up Samuel.

entries.name: Bathsheba
entries.note: Taken by David; mother of Solomon and queen mother.

entries.name: Tamar (David's daughter)
entries.note: Raped by her half-brother Amnon; avenged by Absalom.

entries.name: The wise woman of Tekoa
entries.note: Recruited by Joab to persuade David to bring Absalom home.

entries.name: Rizpah
entries.note: Saul's concubine who guards her sons' bodies from the birds.

entries.name: The queen of Sheba
entries.note: Tests Solomon's wisdom; Jesus says she will rise in the judgment.

entries.name: Jezebel
entries.note: Sidonian queen of Ahab who promotes Baal and arranges Naboth's murder.

entries.name: The widow of Zarephath
entries.note: Feeds Elijah in famine; her son is raised.

entries.name: The Shunammite woman
entries.note: Hosts Elisha; her son is promised, dies and is raised.

entries.name: Naaman's servant girl
entries.note: Captive Israelite girl who points her master to the prophet in Samaria.

entries.name: Athaliah
entries.note: Queen mother who seizes Judah's throne for six years.

entries.name: Jehosheba
entries.note: King Jehoram's daughter who hides the infant Joash.

entries.name: Huldah
entries.note: Prophetess consulted on the book of the law.

entries.name: Gomer
entries.note: Hosea's wife, whose unfaithfulness becomes a prophetic sign.

entries.name: Vashti
entries.note: Persian queen deposed for refusing to appear at the king's feast.

entries.name: Esther
entries.note: Jewish queen of Persia who risks her life to save her people.

entries.name: Mary, mother of Jesus
entries.note: Virgin of Nazareth who conceives by the Holy Spirit; present at the cross and in the upper room.

entries.name: Elizabeth
entries.note: Mother of John the Baptist; filled with the Spirit, she blesses Mary.

entries.name: Anna
entries.note: Aged prophetess in the temple who speaks of the child Jesus.

entries.name: Mary Magdalene
entries.note: Healed disciple and patron; first witness of the resurrection. Western tradition from Gregory the Great conflated her with the sinful woman of Luke 7; the text does not.

entries.name: Joanna
entries.note: Wife of Herod's steward Chuza; supports Jesus and witnesses the empty tomb.

entries.name: Susanna
entries.note: One of the women who provide for Jesus from their means.

entries.name: Salome
entries.note: Watches the crucifixion and brings spices to the tomb; often identified with the mother of Zebedee's sons.

entries.name: Mary wife of Clopas
entries.note: Stands by the cross with Jesus' mother.

entries.name: Martha
entries.note: Hosts Jesus at Bethany and confesses him as the Christ.

entries.name: Mary of Bethany
entries.note: Sits at Jesus' feet and anoints him for burial.

entries.name: The Samaritan woman
entries.note: Converses with Jesus at Jacob's well and brings her town to him.

entries.name: The woman with the issue of blood
entries.note: Healed after twelve years by touching Jesus' garment.

entries.name: The Syrophoenician woman
entries.note: A Gentile whose persistent answer wins healing for her daughter.

entries.name: The poor widow
entries.note: Gives two mites, "all her living".

entries.name: The woman who anointed Jesus in Galilee
entries.note: A "sinner" who washes Jesus' feet with tears in a Pharisee's house.

entries.name: Herodias
entries.note: Wife of Antipas who demands John the Baptist's head.

entries.name: Sapphira
entries.note: Lies with Ananias about the price of their land and dies.

entries.name: Dorcas (Tabitha)
entries.note: Disciple at Joppa full of good works; raised by Peter.

entries.name: Mary mother of John Mark
entries.note: Her Jerusalem house is a place of prayer for the church.

entries.name: Rhoda
entries.note: Servant girl who is so glad to hear Peter that she forgets to open the door.

entries.name: Lydia
entries.note: Seller of purple from Thyatira; first convert at Philippi and host of the church.

entries.name: Damaris
entries.note: Believes after Paul's speech at the Areopagus.

entries.name: Priscilla (Prisca)
entries.note: Tentmaker and teacher who with Aquila instructs Apollos; often named before her husband.

entries.name: Philip's daughters
entries.note: Four unmarried daughters who prophesied.

entries.name: Phoebe
entries.note: Servant (deacon) of the church at Cenchreae and patron of Paul, likely the bearer of Romans.

entries.name: Junia
entries.note: Paul's kinswoman and fellow prisoner, "of note among the apostles" (sense debated).

entries.name: Euodia and Syntyche
entries.note: Women who laboured with Paul in the gospel, urged to agree in the Lord.

entries.name: Lois and Eunice
entries.note: Timothy's grandmother and mother, whose unfeigned faith he shares.

entries.name: Chloe
entries.note: Her household reports the Corinthian divisions to Paul.

entries.name: Nympha
entries.note: Hosts a church in her house near Laodicea.

title: Authors of the Bible
intro: For each book: the traditional attribution (from the text itself, Jewish tradition such as the Talmud's *Baba Bathra* 14b-15a, or early church writers) and the main lines of modern critical scholarship. Many books are anonymous; "traditional" and "scholarly" here are descriptions of views, not verdicts. Conservative scholars defend many traditional attributions with arguments of their own.

entries.name: Genesis
entries.note: Traditional: Moses. Scholarly: a composite of sources or layers (the Documentary Hypothesis's J, E, P, or newer supplementary and fragmentary models), reaching final form in the exilic or Persian period.

entries.name: Exodus
entries.note: Traditional: Moses, who is said to write down God's words. Scholarly: composite, as for Genesis.

entries.name: Leviticus
entries.note: Traditional: Moses. Scholarly: largely the Priestly source and Holiness Code, often dated exilic or post-exilic, though some argue for older material.

entries.name: Numbers
entries.note: Traditional: Moses, who records the stages of the journey. Scholarly: composite with priestly and non-priestly strands.

entries.name: Deuteronomy
entries.note: Traditional: Moses (with the account of his death by Joshua or a later hand). Scholarly: core law code linked to Josiah's reform (7th century BC), framed later.

entries.name: Joshua
entries.note: Traditional: Joshua (Talmud), who "wrote these words in the book of the law of God". Scholarly: part of the Deuteronomistic History, compiled in the late monarchy and exile.

entries.name: Judges
entries.note: Traditional: Samuel (Talmud). Scholarly: Deuteronomistic History, using older hero stories and the Song of Deborah, one of the oldest poems in the Bible.

entries.name: Ruth
entries.note: Traditional: Samuel (Talmud). Scholarly: anonymous; dated to the monarchy by some and to the post-exilic period by others.

entries.name: 1 Samuel
entries.note: Traditional: Samuel, with Nathan and Gad completing it (based on 1 Chr 29:29). Scholarly: Deuteronomistic History drawing on earlier narratives such as the ark story and David's rise.

entries.name: 2 Samuel
entries.note: Traditional: Nathan and Gad. Scholarly: Deuteronomistic History incorporating the so-called Succession Narrative (2 Sam 9-20; 1 Kgs 1-2).

entries.name: 1 Kings
entries.note: Traditional: Jeremiah (Talmud). Scholarly: Deuteronomistic History, citing sources such as the acts of Solomon and the chronicles of the kings.

entries.name: 2 Kings
entries.note: Traditional: Jeremiah. Scholarly: Deuteronomistic History, finished after 561 BC since it records Jehoiachin's release.

entries.name: 1 Chronicles
entries.note: Traditional: Ezra (Talmud). Scholarly: "the Chronicler", a Levitical author of the late Persian period (c. 400-350 BC), probably distinct from Ezra-Nehemiah.

entries.name: 2 Chronicles
entries.note: Traditional: Ezra. Scholarly: the Chronicler, as above.

entries.name: Ezra
entries.note: Traditional: Ezra, with first-person memoirs. Scholarly: Ezra-Nehemiah (one book in the Hebrew Bible) compiled from Ezra and Nehemiah memoirs and Persian documents.

entries.name: Nehemiah
entries.note: Traditional: Nehemiah ("the words of Nehemiah"). Scholarly: Nehemiah memoir embedded in Ezra-Nehemiah.

entries.name: Esther
entries.note: Traditional: Mordecai or the Men of the Great Assembly. Scholarly: anonymous, late Persian or early Hellenistic period.

entries.name: Job
entries.note: Traditional: the Talmud names Moses; others suggest Job himself or Solomon. Scholarly: anonymous, usually dated 6th-4th century BC, with debate over the unity of the speeches of Elihu.

entries.name: Psalms
entries.note: Traditional: David and others named in superscriptions (Asaph, the sons of Korah, Solomon, Moses, Heman, Ethan). Scholarly: a collection formed over centuries; the superscriptions are generally seen as later editorial notes.

entries.name: Proverbs
entries.note: Traditional: Solomon, with sections by "the wise", Agur and Lemuel, and proverbs copied by Hezekiah's men. Scholarly: a collection of collections, some possibly monarchic, finalised after the exile.

entries.name: Ecclesiastes
entries.note: Traditional: Solomon, "the Preacher, the son of David". Scholarly: a later sage writing in Solomon's persona, often dated 3rd century BC on linguistic grounds.

entries.name: Song of Solomon
entries.note: Traditional: Solomon. Scholarly: anonymous love poetry, possibly an anthology; the superscription may mean "for" or "about" Solomon.

entries.name: Isaiah
entries.note: Traditional: Isaiah son of Amoz; the NT quotes both halves under his name. Scholarly: First Isaiah (1-39, 8th century), Second Isaiah (40-55, exilic) and Third Isaiah (56-66, post-exilic).

entries.name: Jeremiah
entries.note: Traditional: Jeremiah, dictating to Baruch. Scholarly: Jeremiah's oracles with Baruch's narratives and Deuteronomistic prose; the Greek text is about one-eighth shorter.

entries.name: Lamentations
entries.note: Traditional: Jeremiah (Greek preface and Talmud). Scholarly: anonymous poems composed soon after 586 BC, perhaps by several authors.

entries.name: Ezekiel
entries.note: Traditional: Ezekiel the priest. Scholarly: broadly accepted as substantially from Ezekiel, with some editorial expansion by his circle.

entries.name: Daniel
entries.note: Traditional: Daniel in the 6th century BC; Jesus refers to "Daniel the prophet". Scholarly: court tales (1-6) earlier, with the visions (7-12) completed c. 167-164 BC during the Maccabean crisis; conservatives defend a 6th-century date.

entries.name: Hosea
entries.note: Traditional: Hosea son of Beeri. Scholarly: mainly Hosea, with Judean editing after Samaria's fall.

entries.name: Joel
entries.note: Traditional: Joel son of Pethuel. Scholarly: authorship accepted; date disputed from pre-exilic to Persian period.

entries.name: Amos
entries.note: Traditional: Amos of Tekoa. Scholarly: mainly Amos; the hopeful ending (9:11-15) is often attributed to a later hand.

entries.name: Obadiah
entries.note: Traditional: Obadiah, sometimes identified (Talmud) with Ahab's steward. Scholarly: anonymous prophet after 586 BC.

entries.name: Jonah
entries.note: Traditional: Jonah son of Amittai. Scholarly: anonymous third-person narrative about the 8th-century prophet, usually dated post-exilic.

entries.name: Micah
entries.note: Traditional: Micah of Moresheth. Scholarly: chapters 1-3 widely accepted; parts of 4-7 often dated later.

entries.name: Nahum
entries.note: Traditional: Nahum the Elkoshite. Scholarly: accepted; written between 663 and 612 BC.

entries.name: Habakkuk
entries.note: Traditional: Habakkuk the prophet. Scholarly: accepted; late 7th century BC; the psalm of chapter 3 may have circulated separately.

entries.name: Zephaniah
entries.note: Traditional: Zephaniah. Scholarly: accepted, with some later additions in the closing promises.

entries.name: Haggai
entries.note: Traditional: Haggai. Scholarly: Haggai's oracles in a third-person editorial frame, 520 BC.

entries.name: Zechariah
entries.note: Traditional: Zechariah son of Berechiah. Scholarly: chapters 1-8 from Zechariah (520-518 BC); chapters 9-14 ("Deutero-Zechariah") from later hands.

entries.name: Malachi
entries.note: Traditional: Malachi. Scholarly: possibly anonymous ("my messenger" as a title), mid-5th century BC.

entries.name: Matthew
entries.note: Traditional: the apostle Matthew (Papias, Irenaeus). Scholarly: anonymous Jewish-Christian author c. AD 80-90 who used Mark; minority defend Matthean authorship.

entries.name: Mark
entries.note: Traditional: John Mark, recording Peter's preaching (Papias). Scholarly: generally the earliest Gospel, c. AD 65-70; the link to Peter is debated but the name Mark is widely accepted.

entries.name: Luke
entries.note: Traditional: Luke the physician, Paul's companion. Scholarly: same author as Acts; Lukan authorship debated but widely held possible; c. AD 80-90 (some date earlier).

entries.name: John
entries.note: Traditional: John son of Zebedee, the beloved disciple. Scholarly: the beloved disciple tradition shaped by a Johannine community, c. AD 90-100; identity of the beloved disciple debated.

entries.name: Acts
entries.note: Traditional: Luke; the "we" passages suggest an eyewitness companion of Paul. Scholarly: same author as Luke; whether the "we" sections reflect the author's presence is debated.

entries.name: Romans
entries.note: Paul (undisputed), written down by Tertius from Corinth c. AD 57.

entries.name: 1 Corinthians
entries.note: Paul (undisputed), with Sosthenes, from Ephesus c. AD 54-55.

entries.name: 2 Corinthians
entries.note: Paul (undisputed), with Timothy; many scholars see a compilation of several letters.

entries.name: Galatians
entries.note: Paul (undisputed); date and destination (north vs south Galatia) debated.

entries.name: Ephesians
entries.note: Traditional: Paul from prison. Scholarly: widely regarded as deutero-Pauline (style, theology, dependence on Colossians); defended as Pauline by many conservatives.

entries.name: Philippians
entries.note: Paul (undisputed), with Timothy, from prison (Rome, Ephesus or Caesarea).

entries.name: Colossians
entries.note: Traditional: Paul with Timothy. Scholarly: disputed; roughly evenly divided between Pauline and deutero-Pauline.

entries.name: 1 Thessalonians
entries.note: Paul (undisputed) with Silvanus and Timothy, c. AD 50; probably the earliest NT writing.

entries.name: 2 Thessalonians
entries.note: Traditional: Paul. Scholarly: disputed because of its eschatology and close literary dependence on 1 Thessalonians.

entries.name: 1 Timothy
entries.note: Traditional: Paul. Scholarly: the Pastoral Epistles are widely judged pseudonymous (c. AD 100) on grounds of vocabulary and church order; defended as Pauline, perhaps via a secretary, by others.

entries.name: 2 Timothy
entries.note: Traditional: Paul's last letter from Roman imprisonment. Scholarly: Pastoral, as above; some see genuine Pauline fragments.

entries.name: Titus
entries.note: Traditional: Paul. Scholarly: Pastoral, as above.

entries.name: Philemon
entries.note: Paul (undisputed), with Timothy, from prison.

entries.name: Hebrews
entries.note: Anonymous. Eastern tradition credited Paul (Clement of Alexandria and Origen with reservations; Origen said only God knows); Tertullian named Barnabas, Luther suggested Apollos, Harnack proposed Priscilla. Modern scholarship regards it as non-Pauline.

entries.name: James
entries.note: Traditional: James the Lord's brother. Scholarly: debated; some see a pseudonymous work in polished Greek, others defend James (perhaps with help), c. AD 45-62.

entries.name: 1 Peter
entries.note: Traditional: Peter, "by Silvanus". Scholarly: debated; many judge it pseudonymous (c. AD 80-90) because of its Greek and setting; others accept Peter with Silvanus as secretary.

entries.name: 2 Peter
entries.note: Traditional: Peter, claiming to be an eyewitness of the transfiguration. Scholarly: widely regarded as pseudonymous (early 2nd century), using Jude; it was among the disputed books in the early church.

entries.name: 1 John
entries.note: Traditional: John the apostle. Scholarly: anonymous; same circle as the Fourth Gospel.

entries.name: 2 John
entries.note: Traditional: John the apostle. Scholarly: "the elder", perhaps the John the Elder mentioned by Papias.

entries.name: 3 John
entries.note: Traditional: John the apostle. Scholarly: "the elder", as for 2 John.

entries.name: Jude
entries.note: Traditional: Jude, brother of James (and of Jesus). Scholarly: debated; some see a pseudonymous work, others accept the brother of Jesus.

entries.name: Revelation
entries.note: Traditional: John the apostle (Justin Martyr, Irenaeus). Scholarly: a prophet named John on Patmos; Dionysius of Alexandria already argued on stylistic grounds that he was not the evangelist. Usually dated c. AD 95 under Domitian.

title: Angels and Heavenly Beings
intro: Scripture names only two angels: Michael and Gabriel. Other heavenly beings appear as categories (seraphim, cherubim, living creatures) or by function (the angel of the LORD, destroying angel, watchers). Fallen beings are included for completeness. Raphael and Uriel belong to deuterocanonical and later Jewish literature, not the Protestant canon.

entries.name: Michael
entries.note: Called "one of the chief princes" and "the archangel"; protector of Israel who disputes with the devil over Moses' body and wars against the dragon.

entries.name: Gabriel
entries.note: Explains Daniel's visions and announces the births of John and Jesus; "that stand in the presence of God".

entries.name: Raphael
entries.note: Appears only in Tobit (deuterocanonical: canonical for Catholic and Orthodox churches, apocryphal for Protestants), where he calls himself one of seven holy angels before God. Revelation's "seven angels which stood before God" are often compared.

entries.name: Seraphim
entries.note: Six-winged beings above the throne crying "Holy, holy, holy"; one touches Isaiah's lips with a coal. The name likely relates to "burning".

entries.name: Cherubim
entries.note: Guard Eden's way, are depicted in gold on the mercy seat, and bear the throne-chariot in Ezekiel.

entries.name: Living creatures
entries.note: Four creatures with faces of man, lion, ox and eagle in Ezekiel, identified by him as cherubim; Revelation's four creatures worship before the throne.

entries.name: Archangels
entries.note: The title appears twice: of Michael and of the archangel's voice at Christ's return. Later tradition lists seven.

entries.name: Watchers
entries.note: "A watcher and an holy one" decrees Nebuchadnezzar's humbling; the term was developed in *1 Enoch*.

entries.name: The angel of the LORD
entries.note: Speaks as God and is addressed as God (Hagar, Moses at the bush, Gideon). Many church fathers and Reformed interpreters see a pre-incarnate appearance of the Son; others see a created angel bearing God's name, as in much Jewish interpretation.

entries.name: Captain of the LORD's host
entries.note: Appears to Joshua near Jericho and tells him to remove his shoes, for the place is holy.

entries.name: The destroying angel
entries.note: Strikes Israel after David's census and the Assyrian camp in Hezekiah's day.

entries.name: Guardian angels
entries.note: Jesus says the little ones' angels always behold the Father's face; Hebrews calls angels ministering spirits for the heirs of salvation.

entries.name: Angels at the tomb
entries.note: One or two angels announce the resurrection to the women.

entries.name: Angel who strengthened Jesus
entries.note: Appears to Jesus in Gethsemane (the verse is absent from some early manuscripts).

entries.name: Angels of the seven churches
entries.note: Each letter in Revelation is addressed to "the angel" of a church; interpreted as guardian angels, as the churches' messengers or leaders, or as personifications of each church.

entries.name: Satan (the accuser)
entries.note: The adversary in the heavenly court of Job and Zechariah; in the NT the devil, deceiver and tempter.

entries.name: Abaddon / Apollyon
entries.note: "Destroyer", the angel of the bottomless pit and king over the locusts.

entries.name: Beelzebub
entries.note: Called "the prince of the devils" by Jesus' opponents; Jesus links him with Satan.

entries.name: "Lucifer"
entries.note: The KJV renders "day star" in a taunt against the king of Babylon as Lucifer. Many church fathers applied it to Satan's fall; most modern commentators read it primarily of the human king.

entries.name: Sons of God (Genesis 6)
entries.note: Their union with "the daughters of men" is read as fallen angels (early Jewish and patristic view, cf. 1 Pet 3:19-20; Jude 1:6), as the line of Seth, or as royal tyrants.
